title: Laser Scans Revealed 23 Hidden Ships on a 3,000-Year-Old Temple
mediaSource: Kition Cyprus Bronze Age temple ship graffiti laser scan archaeology

scenes.title: Twenty-three ancient ships appeared from a nearly blank wall
scenes.narration: High-resolution laser scans of a temple in Cyprus revealed 23 ship carvings that were almost invisible to the naked eye.
keywords: Kition Cyprus ship graffiti laser scan

scenes.title: The researchers were not even looking for ships
scenes.narration: Their goal was to record the temple masonry in three dimensions, but the surface data unexpectedly exposed more ship drawings.

scenes.title: Thousands of years had erased most of the lines
scenes.narration: Weathering left only faint grooves, but changing the virtual lighting on the 3D scans made hulls and sails easier to recognize.

scenes.title: This was not one fleet carved at one time
scenes.narration: The ships appear to have been added over as much as 300 years by different generations of people.
keywords: Late Bronze Age Cyprus ship graffiti

scenes.title: The tradition survived major regional upheaval
scenes.narration: Different vessel styles span the period around the Bronze Age collapse, suggesting maritime culture at the site continued through major change.

scenes.title: Laser scanning revived a 3,000-year-old harbor world
scenes.narration: A few worn lines on stone may preserve the ships that people at this ancient coastal community once saw every day.
